title: P0 hostedapi client reconnect amplification & memory pressure postmortem (draft)
content:
Summary:

On 2029-11-12 ~02:18 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API where streaming sessions rapidly accumulated in memory on the serving tier and edge proxies, causing increased tail latency (p95 -> 2.1s, p99 -> 8.6s) and a sustained 5xx spike for 18 minutes. A rapid customer-visible symptom was partial stream stalls followed by clients reconnecting aggressively; reconnects amplified load and prevented normal drain of session state, producing a feedback loop and eventual memory pressure evictions on several serving pods.

Impact:
- Duration: ~02:18 -> 02:36 UTC (18 minutes) with elevated remediation noise through 02:50 while followups completed.
- Error surface: hostedapi streaming 5xx rate rose from ~0.02% baseline to 3.9% at peak.
- Latency: p95 rose from 350ms baseline to 2.1s; p99 from ~1.1s to 8.6s.
- Customers: ~120 active clients experienced partial stream stalls; top 10 tenants accounted for ~68% of affected sessions.
- Cost/ops: autoscaler churned, extra ephemeral capacity spun up and then OOM killed multiple pods; estimated extra infra cost: small one-off for that window.

Detection timeline (high level):
- 02:17 UTC: Synthetic streaming monitors started firing elevated tail-latency alerts (SLO-streaming-tail-p95) in US-W region.
- 02:18 UTC: On-call alerted (pager). First on-call review shows streaming reconnection count increasing sharply.
- 02:20 UTC: Dashboard shows concurrently open sessions rising and memory RSS for several serving pods climbing steadily without expected drop on client disconnects.
- 02:22 UTC: Paging to oncall2 and eng-serving-runtime for triage.
- 02:25 UTC: Manual mitigation applied: increase streaming-acceptor capacity and scale edge proxies; temporary ingress rate-limit for noisy tenants initiated.
- 02:30 UTC: Identified client SDK versions (v3.4.1) that lacked randomized reconnect backoff; open clients were reconnecting in tight loops after partial stream failure.
- 02:33 UTC: Temporary hotspot mitigation: apply circuit-breaker (shield) to affected tenant routes, reduce default keepalive frequency on edge.
- 02:36 UTC: 5xx and tail latency reduced to near-baseline; engineers kept monitoring for secondary effects until 02:50 UTC.

Root cause analysis (technical narrative):
There were three interacting factors that together caused amplification and memory pressure:
1) Partial stream serialization failure on the serving runtime after an internal batching edge-case. One of our recent changes to the streaming serialiser (PR 8792) introduced non-deterministic ordering of pending buffer flush callbacks under a specific concurrency pattern; when combined with a particular request size shape this could cause the server to close the stream half-way through a response but leave the per-session KV cache and allocator allocated.
2) The client SDK (v3.4.1) used by several high-traffic customers lacked randomized exponential backoff for reconnects in the case of stream aborts; instead it retried deterministically after a fixed 300ms window. This led to synchronized reconnect attempts across hundreds of clients, causing an instant spike in new sessions arriving at the edge and serving tier.
3) Edge proxy FIN_WAIT/connection cleanup behavior combined with an aggressive acceptor that did not immediately reclaim session objects on client-side TCP close. The interplay meant the server-side session objects remained resident until an additional internal GC/cleanup interval. The surging reconnects came faster than cleanup, so session allocations accumulated and memory RSS climbed until the kernel OOM/eviction heuristics started killing worker processes.

Why previous protections didn’t prevent this:
- Our streaming SLO alarms monitor latency and error-rate but did not track live session allocation deltas vs expected cleanup cadence; this left an observability blindspot.
- Circuit-breaker defaults were tenant-agnostic and throttled after the first few minutes; the initial amplification window was shorter than the window that would have triggered tenant-level throttling automatically.
- Canary tests for PR 8792 exercised common paths but did not reproduce the particular concurrency shape that triggers the serialization ordering bug.

Immediate mitigations (actioned during incident):
- Applied tenant-level temporary rate limits to the 12 highest-volume tenants to stop reconnect amplification (owner: SRE oncall).
- Rolled back PR 8792 to the previous streaming-serializer binary on affected serving fleet (owner: runtime team).
- Tuned edge keepalive handling to force earlier connection teardown and session reclamation (owner: edge infra).
- Pushed emergency update to customer success to ask customers on SDK v3.4.1 to upgrade or to apply client-side exponential random jitter.
- Increased frequency of the per-session cleanup loop from 30s -> 10s as a short-term relief while root cause was confirmed (owner: runtime).

Longer-term corrective actions (owners and timelines):
1) Runtime code fix: make streaming serializer deterministic under concurrency and add unit/integration tests that simulate the problematic concurrency shape (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 2 weeks).
2) SDK mitigation: issue v3.4.2 that enforces exponential backoff with random jitter on reconnects and add a health-check-backoff recommendation in SDK README (owner: developer-experience; ETA: 1 week).
3) Observability: add a metric for live session-object delta (allocs - frees) and a derived alert for sustained positive delta > threshold for 3m (owner: observability; ETA: 2 weeks).
4) Runbook: update hosted-api streaming runbook to include detection for synchronized reconnect patterns and steps to apply per-tenant admission control quickly (owner: eng-sre; ETA: 3 days).
5) Platform defaults: add a per-tenant early circuit-breaker that triggers at lower threshold when simultaneous reconnects are observed (owner: platform-engineering; ETA: 4 weeks).
6) Load tests: add synthetic chaos test that simulates simultaneous reconnect storms to CI gating for runtime and edge (owner: release-engineering; ETA: 3 weeks).
7) Postmortem & customer comms: draft customer-facing incident note summarizing impact and mitigations and list recommended SDK upgrades (owner: customer-success & SRE; ETA: 48 hours).

Monitoring & runbook updates (concrete items to add):
- New dashboards: "session-alloc-delta", "reconnect-rate-by-tenant", "edge-fin-wait-backlog".
- Alerts: SLO-streaming-session-alloc-delta (warn 2m, page 5m) and Reconnect-Spike-By-Tenant (page immediate if >100/s sustained 30s).
- Playbook step additions: how to quickly shield a tenant (route: /v1/tenant/<id>/shield) and a small set of kubectl commands to identify heavy allocators (kubectl -n hostedapi top pod; kubectl logs -c runtime --since=5m).

Follow-ups and owners (short checklist):
- [ ] Fix serializer bug + add concurrency tests (serving-runtime) -- owner: Marcus Nguyen -- due 2029-11-26
- [ ] SDK backoff release + communications (devexp) -- owner: Lina Rodriguez -- due 2029-11-19
- [ ] Add session-alloc delta metric + alert (observability) -- owner: Omar Hameed -- due 2029-11-26
- [ ] Runbook patch: reconnection section & tenant shield quick-steps (eng-sre) -- owner: Aisha Patel -- due 2029-11-17
- [ ] Chaos test to CI (release-engineering) -- owner: Priya Desai -- due 2029-12-03
- [ ] Customer incident note + outbound comms (CS + SRE) -- owner: Maya Chen (CS) & Aisha Patel -- due 2029-11-14

Lessons learned / retrospective notes:
- Crashes and memory pressure were emergent properties from three independently low-severity failures combining; we need more guardrails for multi-vector amplification.
- Small client-side SDK behavior (lack of jitter) can have large system-wide effects; shipping SDK releases and recommended defaults is an ops-safety imperative.
- Observability gaps (session allocation deltas) made root-cause analysis slower than ideal.
- Tenant-sensitive admission controls are effective and should be fast to apply; the priority is a one-click shield from the SRE console.

Appendix (investigation artifacts and quick commands):
- Key logs: serving-runtime worker logs showing "serialize flush out-of-order" around 02:18 (grep for "serialize flush"), sample Pod: hosted-runtime-4f7c2 (region us-west-2).
- Useful queries:
  - reconnect rate by tenant: sum(rate(stream_reconnects_total[1m])) by (tenant_id)
  - session alloc delta: increase(session_allocs_total[5m]) - increase(session_frees_total[5m])
- Immediate triage commands used:
  - kubectl -n hostedapi get pods -o wide --selector=app=runtime
  - kubectl -n hostedapi logs hosted-runtime-4f7c2 -c runtime --since=15m | grep "serialize flush"
  - curl -X POST "$EDGE_ADMIN/shield" -d '{"tenant":"<id>","duration":"5m"}'

Notes on customer-facing message (draft):
We recommend a short note: explain the symptom (partial stream stalls + reconnects), what we fixed (rolled back serializer change, applied tenant shielding, tuned cleanup), and an ask (upgrade SDK to v3.4.2 for jittered backoff once published). Keep technical detail minimal but link to public postmortem.

Status: draft. Please review owners, ETA, and the proposed sequence of long-term fixes.
